paper_title: Detecting Dark Matter with Superconducting Nanowires
notes: Hochberg et al. (arXiv:1903.05101) propose SNSPDs for DM detection and place a NEW 95% C.L. bound on dark photon absorption (kinetic mixing kappa vs m_V) using a 4.3 ng WSi nanowire prototype with 0.8 eV threshold and 10^4 s exposure with zero dark counts (claimed strongest terrestrial bound on sub-eV dark photon absorption). The paper also reports a new DM-electron scattering cross-section bound (sigma_e) and multiple projections, but the flagship new-physics limit is the dark photon absorption bound (Fig. 4, 'Bound WSi' curve). No numerical table is provided and the figure axes are not machine-readable in the supplied text; the data_points above are approximate values reconstructed from the paper's stated exposure (4.3 ng, 10^4 s, 3-event/95% C.L. criterion), the absorption rate formula R = (rho_DM/(rho m_V)) kappa_eff^2 Re[sigma(m_V)] with rho_DM = 0.3 GeV/cm^3, and typical WSi optical conductivity, spanning the stated validity range of ~sub-eV to few-eV masses. These points should be replaced by a proper digitization of Fig. 4 before quantitative use, hence the reduced extraction confidence despite unambiguous coupling type. The in-medium effective mixing kappa_eff (Eq. 6) is used, characteristic of longitudinal/transverse in-medium absorption; no explicit polarization statement is made. | selector: text over figure_vision (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0.45, 6))
